maria: Heads-up — ran a long nsys on a 4xA100 job with batching_interleave enabled. Seeing bursty short kernels on GPU0 while others sit idle; looks like an interleave scheduling effect after the kernel selector change (abc1234).

ajay: Which commit exactly? we saw a canary perf dip last night.

maria: commit abc1234 (kernel-chooser:prefetch heuristics). repro is local and consistent. attached a short summary: all-reduce windows end up staggered, rank0 emits many small kernels (1-3ms) and then waits.

sam: Can you paste the nsys command you used?

maria: ```
nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys_out --trace=cuda,nvtx,cudnn --capture-range=nvtx --duration=60 --target-processes=all -- python tools/repro/interleave_run.py --gpus=4 --seq=2048 --batching=interleave
```

ajay: also ran perfetto earlier — NCCL timeline shows serialized allreduces: ranks 1-3 run, rank0 joins late. perfetto link: (internal) perfetto.redwood/s/xyz

jen: Is the KV cache handshake happening at every microbatch boundary? that would serialize across ranks.

maria: Yes — logs show `kv.handshake` NVTX ranges repeated per microbatch for long sequences when batching_interleave=on. handshake duration ~4-6ms on rank0.

perf-bot: Regression alert: p99 latency +7% and throughput -4% since abc1200 -> abc1234 on interleave microbench. See dashboard: /dash/perf/regressions

sam: From flame: hotspots are softmax small kernels, rotary kernels, then an allreduce tail. lots of tiny cudaLaunch calls on GPU0.

ajay: Repro perf command I used: ```
perf record -g -o perf.data -- ./bazel-bin/infer_bench --gpus=4 --seq_len=2048 --batching=interleave
```

maria: Per-GPU breakdown I recorded: GPU0: ~120 kernels in 60s mostly 0.8-2.5ms each. GPUs1-3: ~20 kernels but each 8-25ms. Hypothesis: selector prefers short-kernel path for the first microbatch on rank0, causing downstream allreduce to be misaligned and serialize.

jen: That matches a config I saw: `prefer_short_kernels=true` in runtime-config. Can you toggle to `prefer_throughput` and rerun?

maria: I tried prefer_throughput (disable short-path) — p99 improves ~9% but cost/token +3%. So mitigates but isn't ideal. I pushed a small repro script to tools/repro/interleave_burst.sh.

ajay: Let's capture NCCL trace with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` and set `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` to see queueing/serialization. Also try `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL` for more timeline detail.

maria: Starting a 30s nsys + NCCL debug run now. NVTX shows repeated `kv.handshake` ranges overlapping with kernel dispatch on GPU0.

perf-bot: Note: historical runs didn't show `kv.handshake` at microbatch boundaries for this model config.

sam: Short-term mitigation: coalesce handshake across microbatches (single handshake per batch group) or reuse KV between microbatches. Long-term: make kernel selector aware of downstream collective windows so it doesn't prefer low-latency microkernels that break alignment.

ajay: I'll draft a tiny PR to gate `prefer_short_kernels` behind a runtime flag + telemetry so we can A/B it. :thumbsup:

maria: Uploaded traces to s3: s3://redwood-perf/1918765432/nsys.nsys-rep and s3://redwood-perf/1918765432/perfetto.pbz2. Will attach perf.data too.

jen: If needed we can rollback abc1234 on canary quickly. I'll queue that if regressions persist in dedicated.

maria: Thanks — will triage with the profiler outputs tomorrow 10:00am PST in the perf-sync. Infra-bot: can you reserve the perf GPU cluster for repro (4xA100) 9:30-10:30?

infra-bot: Reserved `perf-stack-4xA100` 09:30-10:30 PST for user maria.

maria: Final note — logs show small NCCL allreduce backpressure on rank0, adding small delays before allreduce reduces skew but is a hack. Plan: short-term handshake coalescing + selector telemetry, long-term: selector rewrite to consider collective windows.
